findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11(A) Eating, Drinking: Observed an employee with gloved hands eating foods over a cutting board. Discussed the need to cease snacking on foods during preparation. Halted the process and asked employee to go wash hands and change gloves. Had majority of staff demonstrate hand washing. Discussed with owner and manager the need to discuss glove use with staff. See that staff understands the need to change gloves between tasks. Owner stated that there is a specific designated area for staff to eat foods outside of the kitchen. 


(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of TOBACCO PRODUCTS only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: There are at least eight employees that handle food inside of the kitchen area and no handwashing was observed. Many employees were instructed to wash hands and performed the handwashing process correctly. Be sure to educate all employees on the frequency and importance of handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.11 Clean Condition. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. Observed a cup being used as a scoop in the bulk sugar container. Also, observed handles inside the bulk containers of flour and cornstarch. See that proper scoops are used with handle extended OUT of foods. 

(B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: The facility was observed storing food in packaging that could expose food to corrosion. There was a container of opened ketchup and Hoisin sauce stored in its original container. Due to the acidity of the food contaminants, the item must be transferred to a different container. Highly acid foods can corrode the interior of aluminum cans, causing a hazard to the food items. Ensure that acidic items are transferred to a different container to avoid corrosion.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. The dish machine’s sanitizer concentration tested at 0ppm (CL). Present operator was well aware of how to maintain the machine and was able to change the empty sanitizing bucket. Once new chemical was added, the operator primed sanitizing agent and then primed rinse agent to insure proper concentration. Owner stated that she is present everyday and testing the machine, however, the bucket was empty from previous days’ use and the lack of chemical residual was missed. 

Ensure that the dish machine is testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to sanitize dishes correctly. 

 After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-502.13 Single-Service and Single-Use Articles, Use Limitation. Observed hiyashi Wakame containers being reused to hold fish and cut pork. Cease use of these containers as one of the ingredients is sesame oil. Sesame is now considered a main allergen and these containers should not be reused. 
(A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be reused. (B) The bulk milk container dispensing tube shall be cut on the diagonal leaving no more than one inch protruding from the chilled dispensing head.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Facility has test strips that were not properly recording the concentration of the dish machine chemical. Test strips were available from various locations. The dish machine test strips were expired in 2024. They were discarded. 

 Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment:
There were leaks observed at the following sinks:
-Hot water faucet of the dish machine room hand sink;
- Both necks of the two faucets at the triple sink. 

Ensure that sink faucets are maintained in good repair and in a leak free condition.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: There was a box of pizza stored directly on top of noodles inside of the walk in cooler. Discussed with the PIC personal storage for employees. The pizza box was discarded to correct the violation. Educate employees on proper storage of personal items. Personal items must always be stored underneath or separate from items intended for public consumption. Ensure that personal items are stored in designated spaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. Hand washing was completed without using a barrier to turn off the faucet. Discussed with staff the proper technique for hand washing. Teach your staff to properly wash their hands. 



(B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There were multiple containers of raw chicken above raw beef in the walk-in cooler. This was previously discussed and was to be followed-up on today. Some foods were moved to accommodate Code.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-202.16 Exterior Walls and Roofs, Protective Barrier. The back storage room (with canned goods) still has some mouse dropppings on the floor. Clean the floor of the back storage area so all droppings are removed. 

Perimeter walls and roofs of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall effectively protect the establishment from the weather and the entry of insects, rodents, and other animals.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics.  The walk-in cooler floor is observed soiled. Operator mentioned that the floor is cleaned on Sundays, but the floor should be cleaned at a frequency sufficient to maintain the surface clean. If it is Friday and the floor is observed soiled, then clean the floor at least twice a week.
See General Comments for discussion of organization. There is too much in this space. Reduce menu or move storage into an additional space. 

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: Due to the significant number of priority and priority foundation violations observed during today’s visit, the person-in-charge (PIC) and employees have failed to demonstrate proper knowledge of food safety and the prevention of foodborne illness. Upon arrival, the plumbing at the kitchen’s handwashing sink was observed in complete disrepair. A large portion of the drain pipe was missing, allowing for wastewater to flow onto the floor and counter below. The facility was not aware of the leak, which brings question to if handwashing is occurring as frequent as necessary. Additionally, the facility was observed bare handing ready-to-eat foods, improperly storing foods in refrigerated units, insufficient food handler certificates, improperly storing foods on the floor (including walk in units and underneath counter tops and prep tables), the lack of time as control records for TCS foods, and low concentrated sanitizer buckets. There will be additional follow-ups scheduled to ensure that the facility is brought into compliance and that the risks that contribute to the spread of food borne illnesses are reduced.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: There are at least eight employees that handle food inside of the kitchen area and the inspectors did not observe any handwashing. There were several missed opportunities for handwashing. There are two sinks in the back of the house - one along the cook-line which isn't functional (see violation #51 for further details) and the other is in the dish room (which lacked hand soap). Discussed with the owner the importance of proper and frequent handwashing, as improper handwashing is the leading contributor to food borne illness. Be sure to educate ALL employees on adequate handwashing. Will follow-up on 4/24/2026 to ensure compliance.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee bare hand battered shrimps that were just removed from the frying station. The activity was ceased and corrected. The employee was instructed to wash hands and use gloves as a protective barrier. Violation corrected on site. Discussed with the owner to educate employees on proper food handling and to never use bare hands when handling ready-to-eat (RTE) foods. Ensure that employees are either using gloves or utensils to handle RTE foods to protect against cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There were no paper towels at the hand-sink in the employee bathroom. Shown to the owner and paper towels were provided to the handsink to correct the violation. Single use paper towels are essential for handwashing. Ensure that all hand-sinks are stocked with paper towels to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment:
The facility is observed to be storing food in packages that expose the food to corrosion contamination, including:
- The facility is re-using aluminum and plastic containers to store food items. After the original food item is used, the facility uses the same container to store new foods such as a can of ketchup, baby corn, bamboo shoots, etc. Highly acid foods can corrode the interior of cans, causing a hazard to the food items. Refrain from using cans or containers after the original item is finished. If wanting to transfer foods to different containers, be sure to use food grade approved containers (which were observed in the facility).

2. The facility is observed to be storing raw meat directly in grocery bags. There was raw chicken placed in a grocery bag that was observed on the floor under a table and another bag of raw meat in the walk-in freezer. Grocery bags are not food grade and should not be used as storage containers for food items, as the bags cannot withstand repeated wash cycles and cannot be sanitized. Cease the use of grocery bags for storage purposes.
Ensure that the use of grocery bags and the re-use of can storage is stopped and obtain food-grade containers/bags. A follow up is scheduled for 5/1/2026 to ensure that cans and grocery bags are no longer being used to store food in.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There were multiple containers of raw chicken above raw beef in the walk-in cooler. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order and that food is protected from contamination during storage, holding, preparation, and display. A reference sheet for proper storage order was given to the owner to post near walk in units. A follow up is scheduled for 4/24/2026 to ensure that storage order has been corrected in the walk-in cooler.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
There were multiple food items observed to be stored on the floor, including but not limited to:

1. There was a sheet pan of blocks of cream cheese and imitation crab sticks observed on the floor under the cook-line. 
2. Multiple pots of sauces stored on the floor under a table. These pots of sauces were under a table to the right of the handwashing sink that has a broken pipe. The waste water leaking from the broken pipe was directly touching the bottom of these pans. This is why it is important that food is stored at least six inches from the ground. 
3. A container of raw chicken in a grocery bag stored on the floor under a table. 

Ensure that food items and container of food items should be stored at least six inches off of the floor.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket in the service station was tested at 0ppm (CL). Discussed with the owner and more bleach was added to the solution. The sani bucket was retested at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that all sanitizer solutions test at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration level.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment:
There are multiple food items in the facility under TIME AS CONTROL that are not being properly marked with the time removed from cold or hot holding, including: 

1. Multiple containers of water that is used for the rice scoop. 
2. Eggs on the cook-line. 
3. Cooked breaded shrimp and chicken that are stored along the cookline

Ensure that the time is being recorded and written down for food items that are removed from cold or hot holding that are under time as control. CORRECTED- A Time as Control policy was filled out during the inspection and this was discussed with the PIC. The facility plans to label food items with tape indicating the time that the food was prepared and will be discarded after four hours if any leftovers are present.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: The facility does not have a probe thermometer available. This was discussed with the PIC. A follow up is scheduled for 5/1/2026 to ensure that a probe thermometer has been obtained. There should always be a probe thermometer in the facility to ensure that foods are being cooked to the correct internal temperature.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: There were at least five unlabeled white bins storing similar white powders in the dry storage hallway. The items are similar in appearance and could be easily mistaken for one another. Discussed with the owner. Ensure that all bins are labeled with the name of the item that’s being stored for identification purposes.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There was about a half inch gap at the bottom of the back door. It appears that the door’s weather stripping is damaged and is allowing sun light through the door. Shown to the owner and she mentioned getting the door repaired. Ensure that all outer doors are tight fitting and never exposed to gaps or cracks that might allow the entry of unwanted pests and/or insects.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were mouse droppings observed on a pan that also stores canned good items in the dry storage area. The owner mentioned that the droppings are old and that she will have the pan removed from the premise. The back storage area is significantly cluttered and could be causing a harboring environment for pest. When time permits, be sure to get rid of items that are no longer useful to the facility. Will follow-up on 5/1/2026 to ensure that mouse droppings have been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There is observed to be a significant amount of food items on the floor throughout the facility, including but not limited to boxes of food in the walk-in freezer, a shelf in the walk-in cooler that is not sufficiently six inches above the floor holding a container of raw chicken, and a box of cans of ketchup under a shelf in the kitchen. All food should be stored at least SIX inches above the ground to protect from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The facility is re-using containers to store food in, including but not limited to, mayonnaise containers and containers that stored seaweed salad and seasoned squid in them. Cease re-using single-use containers to store food in. Utensils and food-contact surfaces should be durable, able to withstand repeated warewashing, and be smooth and easily cleanable. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink in the kitchen had paper towels in the drain at the start of the inspection. The PIC removed the paper towels and stated that the handwashing sink was functional. The inspector began washing their hands using the handwashing sink and the water flowed down the drain and onto the floor. The handwashing sink has a broken pipe that is allowing the waste water to leak onto the table and floor below it. This pipe is observed to be improperly repaired using plastic wrap. A follow up is scheduled for 4/24/2026 to ensure that this handwashing sink has been repaired and is properly functioning.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: There is not any light inside of the sushi prep cooler. Discussed with PIC the need for lighting inside of the cooler. Ensure that lighting is provided to all refrigerated units to allow visibility for food service workers.
findings.citation_text: 6-303.11(B) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (B) At least 215 lux (20 foot candles): (1) At a surface where FOOD is provided for CONSUMER self-service such as buffets and salad bars or where fresh produce or PACKAGED FOODS are sold or offered for consumption, (2) Inside EQUIPMENT such as reach-in and under-counter refrigerators; and (3) At a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor in areas used for handwashing, WAREWASHING, and EQUIPMENT and UTENSIL storage, and in toilet rooms.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Facility could not produce food handler certificates for cooks and other employees that handle food and clean dishes. Employees who are not manager certified must obtain a food handler’s certification if handling food and clean dishes.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink across from the cook line lacked paper towel, handsoap, and a handwashing sign. During the previous original inspection, the owner agreed to convert the sink to a handwashing sink so that employees can conveniently wash hands. An additional follow-up is set for 12/29/2025 to ensure that the sink has been converted to a handwashing sink. Ensure that all handsinks are conveniently located and are stocked with handsoap, paper towels, and a handwashing sign at all times.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: Various violations involving improper handwashing procedures observed today, as well as during previous routine inspections. It is extremely important that proper handwashing is regularly communicated to employees, as it is crucial to food safety and reducing the spread of food borne illness. Improper hand washing is a leading contributor to food borne illness. Employees have been observed washing hands in dump sinks, not using barriers to operate faucet handles after washing hands, and missed opportunities for washing hands after touching body parts with gloved hands. There are two hand-sinks in the kitchen area, however, employees are only utilizing the hand-sink in the dish area. The sink across from the cook-line is used a as dump sink. Discussed converting the dump sink to a handwashing sink, as it is conveniently located for employees to frequently wash hands. A follow-up will be scheduled for 12/26/205 to ensure that hand-sink is proper converted.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(D) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (D) EMPLOYEES are effectively cleaning their hands, by routinely monitoring the EMPLOYEES' handwashing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: At least two employees were observed using bare hands to turn off the faucet handles after the handwashing process. Discussed proper handwashing procedures with the PIC. Educate employees on proper handwashing procedures. When cleaning hands, be sure to follow the following procedures: 1.)  rinse hands with warm running water 2.) apply soap and later hands and arms for at least 10 seconds 3.) rinse soap from hands under running water 4.) use a disposable towel to dry hands (before turning off faucet handles) 4.) use the disposable towel to operate faucet handles to shut off water. Ensure that these cleaning procedures are followed when washing hands to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: The ice scoop’s handle in the bar area was observed in direct contact with the ice. Discussed with PIC that ice scoops should always be stored with the handle faced upward and never in direct contact with ice. Ensure that ice scoops are stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The designated handsink in the bar area was observed with a stainless steel container in the basin area. The facility uses the sink as a dump sink, as well as a handwashing sink. Discussed the need to only use the sink as a handwashing sink. A handwashing sign was given to the PIC to place on the sink. The PIC placed the sign on the sink to correct the violation. Ensure that hand-sinks remain unobstructed to allow proper access for employees to wash hands when necessary. Also be sure that the handwashing sink isn't used as a dump sink.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket in the bar area tested at 0ppm (CL). The bucket contained soap and water. The bucket was re-prepared and bleach was added to the solution (tested at 100ppm CL). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to properly sanitize surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The soda gun holder in the bar area was observed heavily soiled with dried liquids and insects on the food contact surface. Shown to the PIC and the holder was taken apart and cleaned during the inspection. The facility wasn't aware that the holder was able to separate for cleaning purposes. Ensure that soda gun holders are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: There was a container of white rice stored on the counter of the cookline. The facility uses time control to control the safety of the food item, however, the rice exceeded its four hour timeframe. The person-in-charge (PIC) mentioned that the rice was placed on the counter at 11am and the rice was probed at 75F at 3pm. Discussed with PIC that the rice had exceeded its four hour timeframe. The rice was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that foods that are used as time control never exceeds four hours at room temperature. Also discussed keeping track of when food its prepared.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(1) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (1) Except as specified in (B)(2), the FOOD shall have an initial temperature of 5°C (41F) or less when removed from cold holding temperature control, or 57°C (135°F) or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Various food items were stored on the floors of the walk in cooler and freezer. These items include but aren’t limited to shrimp, carrots, frozen meats, etc. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against cross contamination and is at least six inches above the floor at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: There isn’t any light inside of the sushi prep cooler. Discussed with PIC the need for lighting inside of the cooler. Ensure that lighting is provided to all refrigerator units to allow visibility for food service workers.
findings.citation_text: 6-303.11(B) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (B) At least 215 lux (20 foot candles): (1) At a surface where FOOD is provided for CONSUMER self-service such as buffets and salad bars or where fresh produce or PACKAGED FOODS are sold or offered for consumption, (2) Inside EQUIPMENT such as reach-in and under-counter refrigerators; and (3) At a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor in areas used for handwashing, WAREWASHING, and EQUIPMENT and UTENSIL storage, and in toilet rooms.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee in the bar area was observed rinsing hands in the ware washing sink. Educate employees on proper handwashing procedures. When cleaning hands, be sure to follow the following procedures: 1.)  rinse hands with warm running water 2.) apply soap and later hands and arms for at least 10 seconds 3.) rinse soap from hands under running water 4.) use a disposable towel to dry hands (before turning off faucet handles) 4.) use the disposable towel to operate faucet handles to shut off water. Ensure that these cleaning procedures are followed when washing hands to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed touching body parts with gloved hands. The employee was getting ready to engage in food handling before the activity was ceased and corrected. The employee was instructed to wash hands and change gloves to correct the violation. Educate employees on proper glove usage and when to wash hands when contamination occurs.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: A container of raw steak was observed above various sauces in the cooler across from the cook-line. Discussed with PIC and the steak was moved to the bottom shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that raw animal protein is always stored beneath ready-to-eat foods to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
A cutting board that’s being used in the kitchen was observed with several chips on the top surface. Discussed and shown to PIC. PIC mentioned that more cutting boards will be purchased. Ensure that food contact surfaces are maintained in good condition and never with chips or scratches to prevent possibly contaminating food items. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment:
There were leaks observed at the following sinks and dripping into the sink basins: 
- A leak coming from the faucet of the handwashing sink in the kitchen area
- Leaks coming from both faucet heads of the triple sink in the kitchen area

Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that sink faucets are maintained in good repair and in a leak free condition.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Facility could not produce food handler certificates for cooks and other employees that handle food and clean dishes. Employees who are not manager certified must obtain a food handler’s certification if handling food and clean dishes.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: At the start of the inspection, there wasn't a Certified Food Protection Manager available at the facility. Suggested to PIC to get more individuals manager certified. Ensure that a CFPM is present to cover all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed several utensils to be stored with the food contact surface faced upright in the weight station. Discussed with PIC and utensils were taken back to be rewashed and sanitized. Ensure to always store clean utensils with the food contact surface faced down or in a manner that prevents the surface from being contaminated. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the sprayers and the baffles of the hood system to be heavily soiled with accumulated grease. PIC states that facility cleans a couple baffles at a time every Saturday. Inspector suggested to clean baffles and sprayers more than once a week to maintain grease build-up. EMS Hood cleaning services the facility’s hood system every 6 months. Ensure to clean hood system as often as necessary to prevent accumulated grease build-up. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The dump sink in the service station is equipped with paper towel and a soap dispenser. PIC noted that the sink is used only for dumping and that no handwashing occurs at the sink. Discussed having the soap dispenser and paper towel removed from the sink. 

6-301.13: A sink used for FOOD preparation or UTENSIL washing, or a service sink or curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water or similar wastes, may not be provided with the handwashing aids and devices required for a HANDWASHING SINK.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed several containers of food items to not be properly covered in the walk in cooler. Some foods didn’t have a cover at all. Ensure that food items are properly covered during storage to prevent contamination.  

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed food items to be stored in the original can after opening. Discussed with PIC and foods were transferred to different containers and properly labeled. Ensure that food items are transferred to a different container after opening. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the soda gun nozzle to be heavily soiled. Discussed with PIC and nozzle was removed and cleaned. Ensure that soda nozzles are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil buildup. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed several knives stored in between coolers in the bar area. The surfaces of the knives were touching the sides of the coolers. Discussed with PIC and knives were taken back to be cleaned. Ensure that clean knives are stored in a manner that prevents them from contamination. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed several personal food/beverages stored with food intended for public consumption all throughout the facility. Discussed with PIC and food/beverages were removed. Ensure that employee food and drinks are stored separate from products that will be used for public consumption. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.
